summary: Intermittent 403s for private tenant behind VPN split-tunnel due to identity-proxy Set-Cookie path mismatch
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403 Authorization failures for their private deployment when users are connected over company VPN configured with split-tunnel. Impact: Several internal apps using Redwood API return 403s intermittently for a subset of users; affects ability to call inference endpoints and admin console access. Environment: Private deployment (VPC peering), identity-proxy v1.9.3, ingress ALB, customer uses corporate VPN with split-tunnel routing where traffic to some hostnames routes inside tunnel and some goes directly to internet.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer logs into Redwood Console through private deployment (via SSO).
2) From inside corporate VPN with split-tunnel, open app that calls Redwood inference endpoints on /internal-api/* paths.
3) Repeat requests from a machine on VPN and a machine off-VPN; observe intermittent 403s only from some on-VPN sessions.
4) Capture request headers and cookie presence for failing vs successful requests.
expected_behavior: Auth cookie set by identity-proxy is included on subsequent requests from users in the same browser session, allowing authorized calls to inference and admin routes.
actual_behavior: Requests intermittently missing the auth cookie when routed over VPN split-tunnel to certain internal host/path combinations, resulting in 403 Unauthorized from the authz layer.
logs_and_errors: authz service logs: 403 - missing session cookie (session_id)
ingress (ALB) access logs: cookie not present on failed requests; same client IP shows cookie present on successful requests
identity-proxy logs: Set-Cookie sent with Path=/customer/tenant123/internal-api but later requests arrive at /internal-api (path mismatch)
tcpdump from customer: client is not sending cookie on requests that hit internal route rewrite
customer_notes: Customer (Vireo): We only see this for users on VPN and only for our internal app paths. Workaround that helps is forcing all traffic through the VPN (disable split-tunnel) or using a browser private window.
Customer: We cannot disable split-tunnel for all users; need a server-side fix or config change.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial triage (Marina): Collected ingress logs, identity-proxy Set-Cookie headers, and customer tcpdumps. Observed Set-Cookie path was scoped to a tenant-prefixed subpath and not a root path.

2026-03-10 - SRE (Diego): Confirmed failing requests originate from same client IPs as successes; cookie present on some requests but absent on others from same session. Hypothesis: split-tunnel route causes requests to be rewritten/normalized by corporate proxy or by ALB path rewriting, causing cookie path mismatch and client not sending cookie.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Priya): Reproduced locally by setting identity-proxy to emit Set-Cookie with Path=/tenant/abc/internal-api and then requesting /internal-api; browsers do not send cookie when path scope excludes the request path after rewrite. Also found some corporate proxies strip path prefixes in upstream requests which breaks cookie path semantics.
Additional checks: SameSite and Secure flags were set correctly; domain matched. Problem is specifically Path scoping combined with network path rewrite due to split-route behavior.
actions_taken: Applied temporary workaround for customer on 2026-03-11: identity-proxy configuration override to emit Set-Cookie Path=/ (root) for tenant tenant123 in their private deployment. This restored cookie sending for on-VPN clients and removed 403s.
Opened engineering task to implement configurable default cookie path for private deployments and to add a flag preserve_cookie_path=false to avoid tenant-prefixed paths by default.
Requested customer to validate workaround during business hours and confirm 24h stability.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Resolution: Permanent fix merged to identity-proxy to default Set-Cookie Path=/ for private deployments unless explicitly overridden by tenant config (PR: https://github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pull/412).
Deployed patch to customer's private control plane during maintenance window 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC; customer confirmed reduced 403s to zero in subsequent 48-hour window.
Follow-up: Added runbook entry advising customers using split-tunnel VPNs to prefer root cookie paths and documented configuration knob in private deployment docs. Linked confluence page updated.
next_steps: 1) Ship backport to v1.9.x line for customers still on older identity-proxy releases (Engineering).
2) Notify CS/Onboarding to request customers using split-tunnel to validate cookie path behavior during install checks.
3) Add automated test in e2e suite simulating path rewriting to prevent regressions.
